## Human-readable summary

This fixture contains CORRECT code that a prior RDG run incorrectly flagged as a P0 violation. The 2026-03-13 incident (documented in `RDG_GOVERNANCE_REPORTS_PLAYBOOK.md` §False Positive Triage Methodology) found that ~21% of P0 findings were false positives, including this exact shape: returning `{ converged: false }` as a status field.

The prompt-precision fix (per the RDG Authority Doctrine) was to teach the auditor that `converged: false` is HONEST STATUS REPORTING, not a safety net. The auditor must distinguish:
- **Safety net (forbidden):** silently substitutes a default value, hiding the failure.
- **Status reporting (correct):** returns `{ converged: false }` so the caller can decide.

### What this fixture demonstrates
The regression anchor for prompt-precision fixes. If a future prompt revision drops the `converged: false` whitelist, this fixture flips from PASS to (incorrectly) FAIL — and the test runner surfaces the regression.

### What would falsify the fixture (i.e., bring back the FP)
- An RDG run that emits a P0 / P1 finding pointing at the `return { ..., converged: false }` line.
- An RDG run that suggests "throw on non-convergence" as a fix — which would push the policy decision into the wrong layer.

### Why this matters
LLM-auditing-LLM bias is real. Without anchored fixtures for previously-corrected false positives, prompt revisions can silently regress. This is the substrate that makes the False Positive Triage Methodology durable.

### Gating pipeline
`code-health.rdg` (prompts/code-health.md §2 "Safety Net Patterns (HIGH PRIORITY)" and §"Legitimate patterns (NOT safety nets)").
